name: Chandrayaan-3
short_status: Landed 23 Aug 2023 at 69.37 S (Statio Shiv Shakti); Vikram and Pragyan completed one lunar day plus a hop bonus, the propulsion module returned to Earth orbit; full success.
tagline: ISRO · India · Rover · 2023 · The robotic return Success
stats: nation to soft-land on the Moon
landing latitude, first in the south polar region
roved by 26 kg Pragyan in one lunar day

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 14 July 2023, LVM3 M4, Satish Dhawan Space Centre (Sriharikota)

facts.label: Landing
facts.value: 23 August 2023, 18:04 IST; 4th nation to soft-land, 1st in south polar region

facts.label: Mass
facts.value: 3,900 kg total: 2,148 kg propulsion module + 1,752 kg lander module incl. 26 kg Pragyan rover

facts.label: Rover traverse
facts.value: 100+ metres in one lunar day; slept 2 September 2023, never woke

facts.label: LIBS result
facts.value: First in-situ elemental analysis near lunar south pole; sulfur confirmed plus Al, Ca, Fe, Cr, Ti, Mn, Si, O

facts.label: Hop experiment
facts.value: Vikram refired engines, rose ~40-50 cm and moved 30-40 cm; 2026 ApJ paper (Durga Prasad et al., ApJ 1001 135) shows plume stripped ~3 cm of dust, exposing layered regolith

facts.label: Propulsion module return
facts.value: TEI 13 Oct 2023, left lunar SOI 10 Nov after 4 flybys, high Earth orbit (announced 4 Dec 2023); explicit sample-return ops rehearsal

facts.label: ChaSTE headline result (2025)
facts.value: Surface hit ~82 C on a 6-degree sunward slope; model shows poleward slopes >14 degrees at high latitude could harbour near-surface water ice (Comms Earth & Environment, March 2025)

facts.label: Context: Chandrayaan-2 orbiter
facts.value: Still healthy in 100 km polar orbit, payloads operational; new polar data products released November 2025

facts.label: Context: Chandrayaan-4 sample return
facts.value: Cabinet-approved 18 Sep 2024 at Rs 2,104.06 crore; two LVM3 launches with Earth-orbit and lunar-orbit docking, ~3 kg samples; targeted around 2028 (as of December 2025, reaffirmed by ISRO Chairman V. Narayanan), with April 2026 parliamentary-committee reporting flagging launch-vehicle readiness and slow spending as schedule risks

facts.label: Context: Chandrayaan-5 / LUPEX
facts.value: ISRO-JAXA joint mission approved 10 March 2025; ~350 kg JAXA rover on ISRO lander, launch on Japan's H3-24L; JAXA's English project page gives no earlier than 2028 and its Japanese page gives Japanese fiscal year 2028, April 2028 to March 2029 (as of September 2026)

facts.label: Context: Gaganyaan crewed program
facts.value: Uncrewed G1 targeted H2 2026 (as of July 2026): the Feb 2026 window was abandoned, and G1 had not flown as of 18 July 2026, with reporting expecting it around late 2026 carrying the Vyommitra robot; first crewed flight targeted 2027 (as of July 2026), with officials suggesting a possible slip to 2028; crewed Moon landing goal 2040

IAU approves the name Statio Shiv Shakti
ChaSTE paper: warmer surface, possible near-surface ice on steep poleward slopes
Hop-site erosion and regolith layering paper (ApJ 1001 135)
